subject: Extracting Discrete Info from Posterior Trees and Making Transition plots.

messages.author: 09d96c7bbd39063d
messages.subject: Extracting Discrete Info from Posterior Trees and Making Transition plots.
parts:
Hi,
In order to examine the rate of transmission between regions in discrete analysis, I would like to extract discrete info such as dates and inferred ancestral regions from about 1000 posterior trees and then generate within regions transition plots. Please can someone point me to a comprehensive tutorial on how to do this? 

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Extracting Discrete Info from Posterior Trees and Making Transition plots.
parts:
Hi All,

I managed to come up with these codes that should read the .trees beast file and then generate Rdata for plotting  transition between discrete regions, but unfortunately I am getting the "subscript out of bound error". while trying to read them in. Please can Someone advise me on this?

# load tree(s) and extract times of transitions between discrete traits
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtree)

# read in multiple BEAST trees and fortify to get dataframe
beast <- treeio::read.beast('FG_SE_1000.trees').   #This is where I have issues reading my .trees in
class(beast) <- "multiPhylo"
beast_dat <- fortify(beast)

# problem - method leaves no time-calibrated info in trees
# in each tree x = 0 for root and varies for tips - should be other way around
ggtree(beast)

# can sort for plot using mrsd
ggtree(beast, mrsd = "2012")

# use a loop to add dates to convert curr x values to heights
# calibrate nodes using time of most recent sample
n_trees <- length(unique(beast_dat$.id))
beast_dat$height <- beast_dat$x
for (i in 1:n_trees) {
  # select a tree and get the maximum x value for it
  curr_tree_id <- unique(beast_dat$.id)[i]
  curr_max_x <- max(beast_dat$x[beast_dat$.id == curr_tree_id])
  
  # for each row/node subtract curr x from max x for tree - gives a height
  beast_dat$height[beast_dat$.id == curr_tree_id] <- curr_max_x - beast_dat$x[beast_dat$.id == curr_tree_id]
}

# heights can be taken away from the date of the most recent sample to give dates
beast_dat$date <- 2012 - as.numeric(as.character(beast_dat$height))

# we now have region and time at each node
beast_dat$region
beast_dat$date

beast_dat$region <- gsub("UG", "UG", beast_dat$region)
beast_dat$region <- gsub("MG", "MG", beast_dat$region)
beast_dat$region <- gsub("KM", "KM", beast_dat$region)

# create variables for parent node region and date
beast_dat$region_parent <- NA
beast_dat$date_parent <- NA

for (i in 1:nrow(beast_dat)) {
  curr.parent <- beast_dat$parent[i]
  curr.tree <- beast_dat$.id[i]
  
  beast_dat$region_parent[i] <- beast_dat$region[beast_dat$node == curr.parent & beast_dat$.id == curr.tree]
  beast_dat$date_parent[i] <- beast_dat$date[beast_dat$node == curr.parent & beast_dat$.id == curr.tree]
}


# for each row (branch) we now have region/date at each end of branch

# the date of transition falls between the dates of parent and node
# estimate a time using a distribution that tends towards the middle of the time window
beast_dat$date_trans <- NA
for(i in 1:nrow(beast_dat)) {
  fit <- rbeta(1, 6, 6)
  delta_date <- beast_dat$date[i] - beast_dat$date_parent[i]
  beast_dat$date_trans[i] <- beast_dat$date_parent[i] + fit*delta_date
}

# create variables for branch transition and whether or not transition occurs
beast_dat$region_trans <- paste(beast_dat$region_parent,
                                beast_dat$region, sep = " to ")
beast_dat$region_switch <- beast_dat$region != beast_dat$region_parent
table(beast_dat$region_trans)
table(beast_dat$region_switch)

# for each row (branch) we now have species/date at each end of branch
# create variables for branch transition and whether or not transition occurs

## A further class of variables allow for focus on each region/host in turn
beast_dat$region_UG <- NA
for (i in 1:nrow(beast_dat)) {
  if (beast_dat$region[i] == "UG" &
      beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "UG") {
    beast_dat$region_UG[i] <- "within"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] == "UG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "UG") {
    beast_dat$region_UG[i] <- "trans_in"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "UG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "UG") {
    beast_dat$region_UG[i] <- "trans_out"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "UG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "UG") {
    beast_dat$region_UG[i] <- "outwith"
  }
}

beast_dat$region_MG <- NA
for (i in 1:nrow(beast_dat)) {
  if (beast_dat$region[i] == "MG" &
      beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "MG") {
    beast_dat$region_MG[i] <- "within"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] == "MG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "MG") {
    beast_dat$region_MG[i] <- "trans_in"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "MG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "MG") {
    beast_dat$region_MG[i] <- "trans_out"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "MG" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "MG") {
    beast_dat$region_MG[i] <- "outwith"
  }
}

beast_dat$region_KM <- NA
for (i in 1:nrow(beast_dat)) {
  if (beast_dat$region[i] == "KM" &
      beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "KM") {
    beast_dat$region_KM[i] <- "within"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] == "KM" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "KM") {
    beast_dat$region_KM[i] <- "trans_in"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "KM" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] == "KM") {
    beast_dat$region_KM[i] <- "trans_out"
  } else if (beast_dat$region[i] != "KM" &
             beast_dat$region_parent[i] != "KM") {
    beast_dat$region_KM[i] <- "outwith"
  }
}
summary(as.factor(beast_dat$region_UG))
summary(as.factor(beast_dat$region_MG))
summary(as.factor(beast_dat$region_KM))
# tidy and save
rm(curr_max_x, curr_tree_id, curr.parent, curr.tree,
   i, n_trees)
save.image("times_prep.Rdata")

Thank you.
